evidence: Checked environment/assets/seed_data.json (28549 bytes, sha256 a1c65c80...7e83740). It is byte-identical to solution/app/src/seed_data.json, and that hash matches raw-evidence-index.json lines 20, 39 and so on. I ran a read-only Python validator from the scratchpad with -B, so it wrote no cache files. Results: (1) Parse: valid UTF-8 JSON, no BOM, LF only, ASCII only. Top keys: generated_note, stages, candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size, users(10), jobs(3), applications(16), messages(127), notes(3), reads(6). This matches hireops_rules.md section 9 (lines 206-209: people, three jobs with cards in order, messages with one long conversation, a few notes and read markers, candidate wording, page size 30). (2) Referential integrity: no duplicate ids or user emails. Every job's recruiter_id is a recruiter and every manager_id is a hiring_manager. interview_limit values (3, 2, 3) are integers in 1..50. Every application job_id resolves and every stage is in stages. Within each stage, positions are contiguous from 1: JOB-PLAT has APPLIED [1,2,3], SCREEN [1,2], INTERVIEW [1,2], OFFER [1]. Interview occupancy is within the limit for every job (2/3, 1/2, 1/3). No job/email pair repeats (rules 2: the same address can't be added twice). All candidate_email values are well-formed. The one REJECTED card (APP-301) has rejected_from SCREEN and a non-blank reason; no other card carries those fields. candidate_status_labels keys equal stages, and the wording matches the rules 7 table. (3) Messages: all 127 resolve to an existing application and sender. Every sender is a permitted participant under rules 6: a recruiter, the job's own manager, or the owning candidate (0 violations). None are blank, timestamps are ISO-Z and non-decreasing within each conversation. APP-101 has 120 messages, 60 from Rafael and 60 from Noor, numbered (#001)..(#120) in order. That agrees with app_context.md:30 ('120 messages at the start'). APP-201, APP-301 and APP-302 have 3, 3 and 1 messages. (4) Notes: all 3 authors may write on that card (REC1; MGR1 on JOB-PLAT; MGR3 on JOB-DSGN). (5) Reads: all 6 markers belong to a participant, and every read_count is between 1 and the message count. db.js:82-83 maps read_count to ids[...][read_count-1], which never goes out of range. Implied unread: Mei 2 on APP-201, Lena 1 on APP-301, others 0. (6) Candidate accounts: each of the 3 candidate users' emails matches applications whose candidate_name equals the account name (Noor: APP-101 and APP-302; Tomas: APP-201; Lena: APP-301). Seed users, names and roles match instruction.md:17 and app_context.md:10-19 exactly. (7) Synthetic/PII: every email uses the RFC 2606 reserved domains hireops.example, candidates.example and mail.example. Names are generic fictional names, and there are no phone numbers, addresses, DOB or IDs. (8) Credentials: the seed holds no password, hash, token or key. The shared demo password appears only in instructions/app_context, which the skill profile and the internal annotation allow. (9) Injection: a regex scan of every string for markup or script, event handlers, template/SQL syntax, URLs, prompt-injection phrasing and secret patterns matched only benign prose. generated_note points to /instructions/hireops_rules.md, a legitimate public file reference. notes[0] contains a semicolon in a sentence. Minor observations, not defects: (a) Noor's APP-101 read_count is 119 while her own message #120 is the newest, and Farah's APP-301 read_count is 2 while her own #3 is newest. Under rules 6 ('sending a message counts as having read'), a writer might have set 120 and 3. The observable unread/seen state is identical either way, because own messages are never unread and the staff message #119 is covered. (b) Three timestamps repeat across different conversations, which is harmless because ordering is per conversation. (c) Applications carry no created_at; the golden supplies a constant. Adversarial angle: a broken app cannot pass this row through seed content, because the seed is input data. A conforming app that loads the seed literally will not trip on orphan ids, out-of-range read markers, over-capacity Interview, or duplicate job/email pairs that would refuse its own seeding. The template seed is the placeholder "CHANGE_ME"; replacing it is the intended task-specific change. This is static source evidence of the seed's bytes, not a runtime or judge measurement, and none is required for this row.
